experiences.failure_mode: As an independent research reduction, direct vanishing has a dichotomy: for a complete first-order obstruction theory it is equivalent to first-order witness liftability/tangent surjectivity, while for a detector-only obstruction it is insufficient to imply witness lifting.

algebraization, rational coefficient/category safety, monodromy and global continuation remain open

experiences.selected_diagnosis: The H4d1b residual was under-typed: the value of direct obstruction vanishing depends on completeness semantics. After typing, it either restates the first-order target or fails to imply it.
experiences.falsifier_or_attempt: For the exact fixed-witness first-order incidence deformation problem, test whether the registered δ1 is the standard obstruction/connecting map with ker(δ1)=im(dπ_(z0,s0)), and whether coefficient-preserving witness deformation along the fixed branch gives im(dπ)⊆T_s0T. If so, determine whether δ1|_{T_s0T}=0 is equivalent to T_s0T⊆im(dπ), hence tangent equality. Falsify by finding a valid registered H4d1b model in which δ1 governs first-order witness lifting but ker(δ1)≠im(dπ), or a coefficient-preserving first-order witness deformation that is not tangent to the same Hodge branch.
experiences.observed_result: For a complete obstruction theory, first-order lift exists iff δ1(v)=0, while a lift over v is exactly a tangent vector upstairs mapping to v; hence ker δ1=im dπ and δ1 vanishes on the entire Hodge-branch tangent iff dπ is surjective. If δ1 is detector-only, the implication to liftability is unavailable.
